To start using Tusan/Tums for development, follow the instructions on the [homepage](/tums) to install it and set it up as a dependency in your mod or plugin. Tums runs on Fabric, NeoForge and Spigot/Paper and the API is the same on all of them. If you're writing a plugin, also read [Spigot / Paper](/tums/developer/paper).

!((warning This wiki is still under heavy development)[Anything could change])

## Basics

In your mod initializer (works both client and server) register your lexer rules (syntax) and nodes. On NeoForge do the same in your `@Mod` constructor, and on Spigot/Paper in your plugin's `onEnable`.

```java
public class YourModInitializer implements ModInitializer {

	@Override
	public void onInitialize() {
        TumsAPI.getGlobalTusan().registerLexerRule(
            new LexerRule(MyTokenType.HELLO,
                WordedPattern.makeOneWordPattern("hello")
            )
        );

        TumsAPI.getGlobalTusan().registerNode(HelloNode.class);
	}
}
```

Make sure to implement `MyTokenType` and `HelloNode`. Read more about it in the next pages

### What is Global Tusan?
Global Tusan is a singleton instance of [Tusan](/tusan) that is used to register lexer rules and nodes. It is used by Tums and is shared by all other mods. If you want to create your own language, create a new instance of Tusan and use it instead. Read more about it in [Creating your own Language](/tums/developer/creating-your-own)

### What is Tusan?
Tusan in this case is the instance of a language in Tums.

## TumsAPI

`TumsAPI` is the entry point for everything above. It has the following methods:

- `getRegister()` - Returns the registry holding the data (variables, functions, events) of every script that has run
- `addEvent(String name)` - Registers an event name that scripts can listen to with `on <name>`
- `getEventMappings()` - Returns every registered event name
- `blank()` - Returns a new, empty language: no lexer rules and no nodes, not even the Tusan defaults
- `getGlobalTusan()` - Returns the [global language](#what-is-global-tusan) that Tums and every addon share
- `runAllScripts(Path scriptsDir, Tusan tusan, MinecraftEnvironment environment)` - Runs every script file in a folder
- `runScript(Path script, Tusan tusan, MinecraftEnvironment environment)` - Compiles and runs a single script, then registers its data. See [Interpreter](/tums/developer/interpreter)
- `executeEvent(String name, HashMap<String, Variable> variables, MinecraftEnvironment env)` - Fires an event, running every script listening to it with the given variables
